subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard browser Control UI ever receive native device/operator tokens, or should browser injection be limited to configured shared token/password auth only?
rationale: The current PR and its linked issue treat native tokens as native websocket credentials that must not cross into the browser, while the sibling Dashboard auth issue and PR explicitly seek native/operator-token parity for the fast path.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Keep native device tokens out of browser injection, update this PR and the sibling parity item to that policy, and require proof for shared token, password, and no-shared-token behavior.

options.title: Allow native-token Dashboard parity
options.body: Close or redirect this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction, accepting that browser Control UI startup may receive native/operator credentials.

options.title: Design a separate browser identity path
options.body: Pause both drafts until maintainers define a browser-safe device identity flow instead of reusing either shared-secret or native websocket token behavior directly.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Keep native device tokens out of browser injection, update this PR and the sibling parity item to that policy, and require proof for shared token, password, and no-shared-token behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current-main Dashboard endpoint observer and has the strongest recent history in the exact Dashboard auth/window surface that now conflicts with this branch.
